channel.title: Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly (masslawyersweekly.com)

item.title: Employment – Vaccination – Religious discrimination
item.description: Where a U.S. District Court judge dismissed claims brought by two plaintiffs who were denied religious exemptions from the defendant employer’s COVID-19 vaccination policy, the dismissals should be vacated because the plaintiffs have alleged plausible claims of retaliation and religious discrimination.

item.title: Criminal – Sentencing
item.description: Where a defendant has challenged his 87-month sentence and an order requiring him to pay restitution in excess of $2 million, the defendant has not shown that the sentence was procedurally or substantively unreasonable, nor has he shown that the restitution order was excessive.

item.title: Employment – FLSA – Settlement
item.description: Where a U.S. District Court judge granted a defendant’s request for enforcement of a settlement agreement, the judge did not err in concluding that the parties had entered into a valid and binding agreement to settle the plaintiff’s Fair Labor Standards Act claims.

item.title: Commercial – Fraudulent inducement – P&S agreement
item.description: Where a defendant seller of a barge has moved for summary judgment, the motion should be denied because the plaintiff has shown at least a triable issue as to whether each one of the defendant’s alleged misrepresentations concerned facts material to the plaintiff’s decision to purchase the barge.

item.title: Consumer protection – Implied warranty – Chapter 93A
item.description: Where (1) putative class actions were brought alleging defects in the transmissions of certain vehicles and (2) the defendant has moved to dismiss a G.L.c. 93A count brought by one of the plaintiffs, that motion should be allowed because the Chapter 93A claim is derivative of claims for misrepresentation and breach of express warranty that have failed as a matter of law and have been dismissed.

item.title: Jurisdiction – Forum selection clause
item.description: Where a defendant has moved for a transfer to the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware pursuant to a forum selection clause in an operating agreement, the motion should be allowed because the plaintiff cannot show that enforcement of the forum selection clause would violate public policy.

item.title: Proposed cannabis reforms get mixed reviews from bar
item.description: Cannabis lawyers divided over whether measures before the Legislature that would revise state law governing the industry addresses core challenges.

item.title: Lawsuit challenges income tax cut ballot question
item.description: A lawsuit before the Supreme Judicial Court challenges the AG’s summary of a proposed income tax cut ballot initiative.

item.title: MassCourts, eFile system fully restored after disruption
item.description: MassCourts and the eFile system have been fully restored and are operating normally following a Feb. 2 disruption, the Trial Court said on Feb. 3.

item.title: AG reports more open meeting law complaints, and violations
item.description: The number of open meeting law complaints and violations reported to the Attorney General’s Office in 2025 rose above 2024 levels, and many more complaints were sent to public bodies directly.
